key_insight: The gDR-Learner estimates how treatment effects vary across a target population beyond a randomized trial, including settings with incomplete covariate data.
clinical_relevance: This statistical methods study could help assess treatment-effect heterogeneity beyond trial participants; it is not an AI cancer drug discovery study.
method: Combines cross-fitted machine learning with doubly robust estimation to generalize conditional average treatment effects.
Extends estimation to covariates observed only in the trial or a target-population subsample.
Constructs weighted conformal intervals for individual treatment effects under covariate shift.
evidence_signal: In simulations, gDR-Learner had the lowest estimation error among tested methods with complete covariates and outperformed the weighted T-Learner with incomplete covariates; an application reanalyzed the Coronary Artery Surgery Study.
watch_item: Generalization depends on the assumptions needed to link trial and target populations; incomplete covariates remain an implementation challenge.
paper_title: DR-Learners for Generalizing CATEs from a Randomized Controlled Trial
